# Research Findings & Journey Map — RF-001: The Bengali Edition Workflow That Never Starts

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Artifact ID | RF-001 |
| Flow Step | 05 — Research customer workflows (Phase: Problem Discovery) |
| Owner | UXR-001 |
| Upstream inputs | IB-001 (v1.0), IOH-001 (v1.0), PS-001 (v3.0), ICP-001 (v3.0) |
| Downstream recipients | PM-001 (review this run), CSM-001, CRO-001, DES-001 |
| Version | 2.0 (attempt 2 — supersedes v1.0, returned) |
| **Participants interviewed / observed this run** | **ZERO** |
| Overall confidence | **Medium** on workflow *structure*, *sequence* and *failure-point location*; **Low** on every rate, count and duration |
| Evidence quality | **Low** — no primary research, no web/desk research, no CRM, no support tickets exist yet (§2) |
| Gate criteria ("sufficient evidence exists to identify recurring pain points") | **NOT MET EMPIRICALLY.** Met in the weaker sense that pain points are now *specified, located in a workflow, and individually falsifiable*. §10 states the minimum evidence that closes the gate and §9 gives two protocols to get it — one of which needs no participants at all. |

---

## 0. What attempt 2 does differently

Attempt 1 was returned because I self-reported low confidence and low evidence quality on an evidence-led step. I still have zero participants and zero research tooling, so restating the same map in a more confident voice would violate my own permission boundary (*never present a finding as validated when the method doesn't support it*). Instead I changed the artifact's contribution.

| Attempt 1 | Attempt 2 |
|---|---|
| Hypothesized journey map of the *buying* process, derived from PS-001's root causes | Journey map of the **workflow the customer is actually in — a programme/grant cycle, not a buying cycle** — which relocates the decisive moment upstream of any vendor contact (§4, G1) |
| Pain points restated as PS-001's P1–P6 | **Three workflow gaps PM-001's artifacts do not contain**: budget-line timing (G1), the unowned dialect/register decision (G2), and the unmapped verifier workflow (G3) |
| Treated ICP-001 as the input to research | **Challenges ICP-001's filter conjunction as a probable null set** (§7) and proposes a $0, no-recruiting test that can falsify the ICP before we spend the discovery budget on interviews |
| "We need 24 interviews" | A **trace-evidence protocol** (§9.1) that answers the two highest-value questions from public artefacts without recruiting anyone, ordered *before* interviews because it is cheaper, faster, and unbiased by self-report |
| Price framed as a value/cost question | Price reframed as an **authority-threshold** question, with a predicted cliff rather than a slope (§6, PP-07) |

If reviewers accept only one thing from this artifact, it should be §7 (the ICP may be empty) followed by §4/G1 (we are selling into a budget-writing moment, not a purchase moment).

---

## 1. Research question as posed

> *How do organizations that own English content and have a Bengali-speaking audience currently get (or fail to get) a Bengali edition produced, and where does that workflow break?*

Sub-questions carried from upstream:

- Q-A: What do they do *instead* today? (alternatives-in-use)
- Q-B: Where exactly does the project die, and who kills it?
- Q-C: Is PM-001's P3 (quality unverifiable) actually the top recurring pain, or is that a plausible narrative? (PS-001 §3 weights P2/P3 at 25% each on the author's own admission that these are hypotheses)
- Q-D: Does the ICP-001 segment exist in usable numbers?

None of these are answered with evidence in this run. All four are now *instrumented*.

---

## 2. Method actually used — stated plainly

**FACT:** The only inputs I could read this run were the four upstream artifacts. No interviews were conducted. No participant was recruited, contacted or observed. No survey ran. No usability test ran. No support tickets, analytics, CRM records or prior research exist, because the company has no customers and no prior research rounds.

**Method actually applied:** structured analogical workflow reconstruction. I decomposed the task ("get a Bengali edition made and delivered") into the decision and hand-off sequence any resourced organization must traverse, and populated each step from model-internal prior knowledge of adjacent, better-documented workflows (nonprofit programme/grant budgeting, institutional vendor procurement, freelance translation engagements, localization vendor management, volunteer review processes). I then marked each step with the evidence status of my claim about it.

**What this method is good for:** identifying *where* in a sequence a workflow can break, and generating discriminating questions. It reliably produces the right **shape**.

**What this method cannot do, and I am not claiming it does:** establish that this is what Bengali-mandate organizations actually do, how often each break occurs, or which break dominates. Every rate, count, duration and price in this artifact is an ESTIMATE from judgement, not a measurement. A well-shaped map with invented magnitudes is exactly the artifact that gets mistaken for evidence three steps later, so every table below carries an evidence column and I have not removed a single "Low".

**Bias I am carrying and flagging against myself:** analogical reconstruction is systematically biased toward *plausible, orderly* workflows. Real workflows are more often decided by one person's idiosyncratic prior experience ("we used a guy my colleague knew in Dhaka last time"). My map probably over-represents rational process and under-represents personal-network shortcuts. PP-03 in §6 is my attempt to price that in; interviews should specifically hunt for it.

---

## 3. The single most important structural finding

**INFERENCE (Medium confidence, and it reframes the step):** There is no "Bengali edition buying journey" to research, and that is why no evidence about it exists anywhere.

The organizations in scope are not in a purchasing process that stalls. They are in an **annual programme and funding cycle** in which "Bengali version of X" is one candidate line item among fifty, competing for space in a budget narrative written months before any work happens. The item is not rejected by a buyer after evaluating vendors. It is **never written down**, silently, by a person drafting a proposal at 11pm who has no idea what it would cost, no way to justify the number, and a hard page limit.

Consequences that matter more than anything else in this artifact:

1. **The decisive moment is upstream of purchase intent.** By the time someone requests a quote, we have already won most of the way. Our funnel problem is not conversion; it is *presence at budget-drafting time*.
2. **The market looks empty because the loss is invisible.** Nobody logs a project they didn't propose. This explains the total absence of market evidence PS-001 and IOH-001 both struggled with — it is not that the data is hard to find, it is that the event leaves no trace on the buyer's side. (It does leave a trace on the *funder's* side — see §9.1.)
3. **PS-001's P1–P6 are reasons, not moments.** They are all real, but they operate at different stages, and two of them (P2 unquantifiable, P5 coordination cost) do their damage at budget-drafting, before any product we build is ever seen. A product that only attacks P3 (verification) and P5 (coordination) at *quote* stage arrives after the deal was already lost.

---

## 4. Current-state journey map — the Bengali edition that doesn't happen

Nine stages. "Attrition" = ESTIMATED share of organizations entering that stage who never reach the next one. Attrition figures are a judgement funnel, **method: subjective staged decomposition of a 100-organization cohort, no data**; they are here to force ranking and to be overwritten by real numbers, not to be quoted.

```
S1 Mandate exists ──► S2 Someone voices it ──► S3 Internal capacity scan ──► S4 Cost discovery
   (100)                  (~45)                    (~30)                        (~20)
                                                       │                           │
                                          [DIES: "our Dhaka                [DIES: no number
                                           office can do it"]               → no line item]
                                                                                   │
S5 Budget line drafted ──► S6 Award & mid-cycle activation ──► S7 Vendor selection ──► S8 Production
   (~9)                       (~6)                                (~5)                    (~4)
        │                          │                                   │                     │
 [DIES: cut for   [DIES: reprioritized, staff turnover]   [DIES: no verifier,   [DIES: dialect/register
  page/priority]                                            no trust]            dispute, rework, stall]
                                                                                       │
                                                            S9 Delivered & read ──◄─────┘
                                                               (~1–2)
```

| # | Stage | What the person is actually doing | Who is doing it | Duration (ESTIMATE) | Emotional state | Dominant pain | Attrition here (ESTIMATE) | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | **Latent mandate** | Nothing. A Bangladesh/West Bengal audience is in the programme logframe; the English asset exists | Programme lead | Continuous | Neutral / unaware there's a decision to make | — | 55% never voice it | Low |
| S2 | **Someone voices it** | Raises "shouldn't this be in Bengali?" in a team call, usually triggered by a field visit, a partner complaint, or a funder question | Programme or comms lead | 1 meeting | Mildly motivated, no ownership | No owner assigned; it becomes an unassigned to-do | 33% | Low |
| S3 | **Internal capacity scan** | Asks around: does anyone speak Bengali? Do we have a partner who could? | Same person, informally | 1–2 weeks | Relieved if yes | **If a local office/partner exists, project exits our market permanently** (ICP-001 F3) | 33% | Low–Medium (structurally near-certain that this scan happens; its *outcome distribution* is unknown) |
| S4 | **Cost discovery** | Googles "Bengali book translation cost", maybe emails one agency, maybe asks a diaspora contact. Gets either silence, a per-word quote they can't convert into a project total, or a wildly variable range ($400 to $9,000) | Same person | 1–4 weeks, low intensity | **Confused, then discouraged** | **No defensible number → nothing quotable to put in a budget (G1)**; price variance of >10× reads as "this market is not legible" | 55% | Low–Medium |
| S5 | **Budget line drafted** | Writes (or omits) a line in a proposal budget + narrative justification | Proposal writer / grants officer, *often not the same person as S2* | Fixed calendar window, 2–6 weeks/yr | Triaging, ruthless | **Cannot justify the line without a forecast reader/impact number (PS-001 P2)**; hand-off from S2 to a different person loses context | 33% | Low–Medium |
| S6 | **Award, then mid-cycle activation** | 3–9 months later, money exists. Someone must remember and restart | Programme lead | 3–9 month gap | Overloaded; item is now #40 of 50 | Staff turnover and reprioritization; the champion may have left | 33% | Low |
| S7 | **Vendor selection & trust** | Needs to choose. Cannot evaluate Bengali. Seeks a person to vouch (ICP-001 §2.2) | Programme lead + borrowed verifier | 2–8 weeks, **highly variable** | Risk-averse, reputationally exposed | **Verifier non-response / latency (G3)**; unhedgeable quality risk (P3) | 20% | Low–Medium |
| S8 | **Production & review** | Manages a chain of 5–7 unfamiliar vendors, or one vendor they can't supervise | Programme lead as accidental project manager | 2–6 months | Anxious, out of depth | **Nobody owns the dialect/register/transliteration decision (G2)**; rework loops; Indic typography failures discovered late | 20% | Low–Medium |
| S9 | **Delivered & actually read** | Publishes/hands out. Usually cannot report readership | Programme + comms | Ongoing | Quiet dissatisfaction | No outcome evidence → the line item is *harder* to renew next cycle, not easier | — | Low |

**INFERENCE (Medium):** the two largest single losses (S4 and S5) both occur **before we would ever have a conversation**, and neither is caused by our price being too high. They are caused by there being **no quotable, defensible number and no forecastable outcome** at the moment a budget is written. This is consistent with PS-001's reframe but locates it in time, which PS-001 does not.

---

## 5. The three workflow gaps (new findings)

### G1 — The budget-line timing gap *(highest commercial leverage)*

**INFERENCE, Medium confidence.** ICP-001's F2 requires a *funded* mandate. Funded mandates in this segment overwhelmingly originate in grant or annual-plan budgets that are fixed at drafting time. Therefore:

- A project not written into the budget cannot be paid for mid-cycle **unless it falls under a discretionary signature threshold** that requires no reallocation approval.
- The addressable moment per organization per year is roughly **2–6 weeks** (proposal drafting), not "whenever we call them."
- What the drafter needs is not a pitch. It is a **paste-able line item**: a fixed all-in price, a scope sentence, a delivery duration, and one citable justification sentence. Anything requiring a conversation arrives too late.
